Here’s what was in place and what changed.

### Before
- Compose used **`portainer/portainer-ce` with no tag**, so Docker resolves that to **`latest`** on each pull. Everything else (ports, socket mount, data volume via env vars) is unchanged.

### After
- Image is pinned to **`portainer/portainer-ce:2.39.2`**, which matches [Portainer’s latest GitHub release](https://github.com/portainer/portainer/releases/latest) (**2.39.2 LTS**) and exists on Docker Hub.

```3:5:/Users/lap14820/Documents/Project/Out/novapo-docker/portainer/docker-compose.yml
  portainer:
    image: portainer/portainer-ce:2.39.2
    restart: always
```

### Apply the upgrade
From the `portainer` directory (with your `.env` or exported variables as today):

`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`

Portainer upgrades are usually in-place on the existing `/data` volume; skim [release notes](https://docs.portainer.io/release-notes) if you’re jumping several major versions.
